entities.name: Internal Reconnaissance
entities.evidence: CISA’s Incident Response team observed these specific techniques leveraged during the agency’s incident response engagements, along with the native tools and libraries to conduct internal reconnaissance and compromise domains behind the Ivanti appliances.

entities.name: Domain Compromise
entities.evidence: CISA researchers assess that threat actors are able to use the credentials to move deeper into the environment.

entities.name: Credential Exfiltration
entities.evidence: Users who currently have active sessions to the appliance could have their base64 encoded active directory cleartext passwords, in addition to the New Technology LAN Manager (NTLM) password hashes, retrieved with the same access, as shown in Figure 10, APPENDIX A.

entities.name: Persistence Mechanism
entities.evidence: The root-level access allows adversaries to maintain persistence despite issuing factory resets and appliance upgrades while deceiving the provided integrity checkers, creating the illusion of a clean installation.

entities.name: Integrity Check Bypass
entities.evidence: bypass integrity checks used by the Integrity Checker application.
